messages:
morgan: quick q — running short nsys captures (10s) for KV-cache profiling and keep missing late OSRT NVTX ranges. capture flags I'm using below. any obvious mistakes?

```
nsys profile -o kv_short.nsys --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --duration=10s 
# also trying sample-window=200ms and default sampling
```

jia: 10s is tiny for workloads with long tails. if your batched requests have retries or queueing you lose tails. i'd bump to at least 30-60s when debugging kernel timelines. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ryan: also: --capture-range=nvtx only records between NVTX push/pop. if some OSRT ops run outside annotated regions you'll miss them. try leaving capture-range off once to get full timeline.

anjali: FWIW we saw OSRT short-run artifacts because sampling interval + short run = aliasing. try disabling sampling (use full tracing) for a short end-to-end run, or increase sample-window and duration. sampling is approximate.

morgan: good points. when you say "disable sampling" do you mean drop --sample-window? i haven't found a `--no-sample` flag in newer nsys.

jia: the flag varies by version. in some builds `--sample=none` works, in others you omit sampling args entirely. check `nsys --help` on the host. but practically: full tracing (no sampling) + longer duration = bigger .nsys file but clear kernel timeline.

ryan: another trick: narrow the process filter so nsys focuses on our runtime pid. `--process-scope` + pid reduces noise. for KV-cache hotness you want GPU kernel timeline + NVTX ranges from the runtime process.

morgan: nice. sharing a quick checklist i used to capture a reliable KV/OSRT trace: 
- run a warmup for 30s to get stable batching
- capture 60s with `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt` and no capture-range
- set process filter to runtime pid with `--process-scope`
- if file size is huge, try `--sample-window=500ms` but *only* after verifying full trace shows the hotspots

anjali: also look out for NVTX bracket granularity — we sometimes push/pop inside tight loops which creates lots of tiny ranges. those get collapsed or sampled away. increase NVTX granularity (coarser brackets) or group ranges: NVTX_PUSH("kv_batch") around the whole batch rather than per-token.

morgan: here's a variant command i'm going to run now (posting for reproducibility):

```bash
nsys profile -o out/kv_kvtrace_v2.nsys \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --duration=60s \
  --process-name=my-runtime-bin \
  --cpuctxsw=disable \n  # (note: --process-name is shorthand; we actually use --process=PID in script)
```

ryan: small nit: use `--force-overwrite true` in CI to avoid interactive prompts. and add `--stats=true` if you want summary tables in the capture file.

morgan: thanks — will try and post the timeline if anything surprising shows up. aiming to validate kernel selection heuristics vs. kv hit rate.

nsys-bot: reminder: large captures (>2GB) can be slow to open in UI. consider `nsys export` to CSV slices or use `--output=timeline.sqlite` and query slices.

jia: last note — when comparing runs (before/after perf regression) keep the same capture method. mixing sampling vs full trace invalidates direct timeline comparisons.

morgan: solid. if this fails i'll trim a minimal repro and ping for pair-debug. thanks all :heart:
